title: UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration

content.overview: The UNCITRAL Model Law on International Commercial Arbitration is a legislative model designed to help States reform and modernize arbitral procedure for international commercial disputes. UNCITRAL adopted the original text in 1985 and amendments in 2006. It is not itself an Indian enactment or a set of institutional arbitration rules.
content.glance: A model for national arbitration legislation: agreement, tribunal composition and jurisdiction, court intervention, and recognition and enforcement of awards. Distinguish the 1985 text, the 2006 amended version and the applicable national enactment.
content.study:
Purpose and legal character: UNCITRAL designed the Model Law to assist States in reforming and modernizing arbitral procedure to meet the particular needs of international commercial arbitration. A Model Law supplies a legislative model; the applicable national enactment must be identified before advising on legal rights or remedies.

Coverage: The official overview describes the full arbitral process, beginning with the arbitration agreement, composition and jurisdiction of the tribunal and extent of court intervention, and continuing to recognition and enforcement of the award. This topic is an overview, not an article-by-article statement of every condition or remedy.

Versions: The original Model Law dates from 1985. On 7 July 2006 UNCITRAL adopted amendments to articles 1(2), 7 and 35(2), a new chapter IV A replacing article 17, and a new article 2 A. UNCITRAL identifies the amended text as the standard version from 2006 while retaining the original because many national enactments are based on it.

Main amendment themes: Revised article 7 modernizes the form required of an arbitration agreement to reflect international contracting practice. Chapter IV A provides a more comprehensive regime for interim measures supporting arbitration. The other identified amendments need review of the official text before their detailed rules are stated.

India and application limits: UNCITRAL's enactment-status page lists India with the year 1996 under legislation based on or influenced by the Model Law. This supports a historical influence statement, not an assertion that every Indian provision reproduces the Model Law or its 2006 amendments. Check the actual national statute, amendments and applicable version. Existing Indian case summaries below are retained for separate verification and are not proof of the Model Law's text.

sections.heading: Purpose and legislative character
sections.body: The Model Law assists States in reforming and modernizing arbitral procedure for international commercial arbitration. It is a legislative model, not an Indian statute or an institutional procedural rulebook.

sections.heading: Coverage of the arbitral process
sections.body: Its coverage runs from arbitration agreements, tribunal composition and jurisdiction, and the extent of court intervention to recognition and enforcement of arbitral awards. Detailed conditions require the relevant official articles and implementing national law.

sections.heading: 1985 text and 2006 amended version
sections.body: On 7 July 2006 UNCITRAL amended articles 1(2), 7 and 35(2), replaced article 17 with chapter IV A, and introduced article 2 A. The amended text is UNCITRAL's standard version from 2006; the original remains available because national enactments may be based on it.

sections.heading: Agreement form and interim measures
sections.body: UNCITRAL's overview explains that revised article 7 modernizes the form of arbitration agreements in line with international contract practice, while chapter IV A establishes a more comprehensive interim-measures regime. Do not infer the precise national requirements from these themes alone.

sections.heading: National enactment and Indian context
sections.body: The official status page lists India 1996 as legislation based on or influenced by the Model Law. Apply the relevant national enactment rather than treating the Model Law as automatically operative or assuming adoption of every 2006 amendment. Domestic current-law and existing-case verification remain open.

provisions.title: Model legislation - overview, not a domestic enactment

examples.title: Legislative reform example
examples.body: A State considers modernizing its international commercial arbitration legislation. The Model Law supplies a framework spanning the arbitration agreement, tribunal and court roles, and award recognition and enforcement; the legislature must decide the enacted text.

examples.title: Version-selection example
examples.body: A student compares an enactment based on the 1985 text with the 2006 Model Law. The student checks which agreement-form and interim-measures changes were actually enacted rather than attributing every later Model Law amendment to that jurisdiction.

examples.title: Indian application boundary
examples.body: A litigant relies solely on the amended Model Law to seek a domestic remedy. India's entry in UNCITRAL's status table establishes influence, not the precise entitlement. Identify the applicable Indian enactment and operative provision before concluding that relief is available.

hypotheticals.question: Does a jurisdiction's entry in UNCITRAL's enactment-status table prove that its legislation copies every 2006 Model Law provision?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The table covers legislation based on or influenced by the Model Law. Identify the jurisdiction's enacted text and amendments and compare the relevant rule; do not equate a listed year with wholesale adoption.

hypotheticals.question: How should an exam answer explain the 2006 update without inventing article-level conditions?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify the amendment date and affected articles, then explain the officially stated agreement-form and interim-measures themes. Reserve detailed conditions and remedies for review of the official articles and implementing national law.

distinctions.title: Model Law and national arbitration legislation

rows.left: A legislative model designed to assist States with reform.
rows.right: The enacted national law must be identified for operative rights and remedies.

rows.left: Original 1985 text and amended 2006 standard version.
rows.right: May be based on or influenced by a Model Law version, with national changes.

rows.left: A source for comparative analysis and legislative design.
rows.right: Check the actual provision, scope, amendments and procedural stage before advising.

misconceptions.trap: The Model Law is itself an Indian statute.
misconceptions.correction: It is a UNCITRAL legislative model. India's status-table entry indicates legislation based on or influenced by it.

misconceptions.trap: The 2006 amendments automatically alter every national arbitration enactment.
misconceptions.correction: Check national adoption and amendments separately. UNCITRAL retains the original 1985 text because many enactments are based on that version.

misconceptions.trap: A Model Law overview establishes a particular domestic remedy or verifies Indian case summaries.
misconceptions.correction: Article-level requirements, national current law and judgment propositions need their own source checks; the overview does not verify them.

cases.name: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
cases.facts: The Court considered arbitrability and the role of the referral court.
cases.issue: When should a court refer parties to arbitration and which disputes are non-arbitrable?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Referral scrutiny is limited, but the court must reject inherently non-arbitrable disputes and examine the arbitration agreement at the statutory threshold.
cases.holding: The Court formulated the modern Indian framework for arbitrability and referral.
cases.relevance: Use for arbitration agreement, referral and jurisdictional threshold questions.

cases.name: Perkins Eastman Architects DPC v. HSCC (India) Ltd.
cases.facts: The dispute concerned unilateral appointment power vested in an interested party.
cases.issue: Whether a person interested in the outcome may unilaterally appoint the sole arbitrator.
cases.ratioDecidendi: A person rendered ineligible to act as arbitrator cannot control the appointment process in a manner that creates justifiable bias.
cases.holding: The unilateral appointment mechanism was held invalid in the circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for independence, impartiality and appointment challenges.

cases.name: Afcons Infrastructure Ltd. v. Cherian Varkey Construction Co. (P) Ltd.
cases.facts: The Court examined court-referred ADR under CPC s. 89.
cases.issue: How should courts select an appropriate ADR process?
cases.ratioDecidendi: The statutory ADR options must be applied according to the nature of the dispute and consent requirements.
cases.holding: The Court clarified the working scheme of CPC s. 89 and Order X.
cases.relevance: Use for mediation, conciliation and court-referred ADR.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the legal character and purpose of the UNCITRAL Model Law?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: It is a model for national legislation designed to assist States in reforming and modernizing arbitral procedure for international commercial arbitration. The original text dates from 1985, with amendments adopted in 2006. It is not itself an Indian enactment.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Source-grounded overview; distinguish legislative influence from operative national law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a submission distinguish the Model Law from the applicable domestic rule?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: First identify the relevant national enactment and operative provision. State the Model Law version used for comparison and explain its legislative influence without assuming verbatim adoption. Check the domestic amendments and procedural stage independently. Do not use the retained, unverified Indian case summaries as proof of Model Law text.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Application method, not a verified pleading for any particular dispute.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What themes did the 2006 amendments address?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: UNCITRAL identifies revised article 7 as modernizing the form required of arbitration agreements, and chapter IV A as a more comprehensive regime for interim measures. The amendment package also affects articles 1(2) and 35(2) and introduces article 2 A. Detailed conditions require the official text.
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: The official overview supports amendment identification and themes, not an exhaustive article-level analysis.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: The Model Law is a legislative model for international commercial arbitration, not itself an Indian statute. Its official overview covers the arbitral process from agreements, tribunal composition and jurisdiction, and court intervention to award recognition and enforcement. UNCITRAL adopted amendments on 7 July 2006 and identifies the amended text as its standard version. The stated themes include modernized arbitration-agreement form and a more comprehensive interim-measures regime. The status page lists India 1996 as based on or influenced by the Model Law, but national provisions and amendments must be checked separately. This batch does not verify every Model Law article, Indian current law or the retained cases.

shortAnswer.prompt: What is the UNCITRAL Model Law?
shortAnswer.answer: A model for national international-commercial-arbitration legislation, adopted in 1985 and amended in 2006, covering the process from agreement and tribunal formation to award recognition and enforcement.
shortAnswer.method: State character, chronology and scope; do not call it a directly operative Indian enactment.

sixteenMark.application: Explain why a model addressing international commercial arbitration helps States modernize procedure while distinguishing model text from enacted law.
